criticalWitness.title: 晉書斠注 七十一v109–110
criticalWitness.quote: 《晉書》校文五曰《御覽》七百四十四引前燕錄作誓不殺汝詳語意崔錄似得其眞又攷《通鑑》作恨恨不欲殺汝注恨恨相戀之情與誓字語意正合此語温公必有所本疑恨不殺汝四字卽恨恨不欲殺汝一語之譌脫

contextUnits.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。

translations.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.

contextUnits.zh: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。

translations.literal: Having then fled, Gui thereupon sent fierce cavalry over a hundred to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.

contextUnits.zh: 翰遙謂追者曰：「吾既思戀而歸，理無反面。

translations.literal: Han from afar told the pursuers: “I already long to return; in principle there is no turning back.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted to them, “I mean to go home—I will not turn back.

contextUnits.zh: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。

translations.literal: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.
translations.idiomatic: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.

translations.literal: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
translations.idiomatic: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.

contextUnits.zh: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；

translations.literal: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if my shot hits, you then should turn back;
translations.idiomatic: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;

translations.literal: if not center, you may come forward.”

contextUnits.zh: 歸騎解刀豎之，翰一發便中刀鐶，追騎乃散。

translations.literal: Gui’s riders undid a blade and set it up; Han one shot then hit the blade ring; pursuing riders then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: They fixed a blade; his first arrow struck the ring and they broke off the chase.

translations.literal: Having arrived, Huang greatly added favor and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Huang welcomed him with rich honors.

contextUnits.zh: 建元二年，從皝討宇文歸，臨陣為流矢所中，臥病積時。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he followed Huang to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle he was struck by a stray arrow; he lay ill a long time.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan, he joined the war on Yuwen Gui, took a stray shaft, and lay long ill.

contextUnits.zh: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。

translations.literal: Later illness gradually improved; at his home mounted horse to test himself; someone reported Han privately practiced riding, suspected as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as his illness gradually improved, he tried riding at home to test himself; someone reported that Han was privately practising riding and suspected something extraordinary.

translations.literal: Huang had long been jealous of him; thereupon granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, who had long been jealous of him, thereupon granted him death.

contextUnits.zh: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。

translations.literal: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; the crime is too great for death to atone; I could not cast my bones in the bandit court; therefore I returned to submit to the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: Nearing death Murong Han told the envoy, “Han harbored distrust and fled abroad; my crime is too great for death to atone; I could not leave my bones in a rebel court, so I returned to submit to the authorities.

contextUnits.zh: 天慈曲湣，不肆之市朝，今日之死，翰之生也。

translations.literal: Heaven’s kindness bent pity, did not display me in the marketplace; today’s death is Han’s life.
translations.idiomatic: The king spared me a public execution—this death is mercy.

contextUnits.zh: 但逆胡跨據神州，中原未靖，翰常克心自誓，志吞醜虜，上成先王遺旨，下謝山海之責。

translations.literal: But the rebellious Hu occupy the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified; Han has always steeled his heart and sworn an oath, intent on swallowing up the vile enemies, above to fulfil the late king's last instructions and below to discharge his duty to the land of mountains and seas.
translations.idiomatic: But the rebel Hu barbarians straddle and hold the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified. I always steeled my heart and swore that I would swallow up the vile caitiffs, above to fulfil the late king's dying wish and below to discharge my duty to the realm between the mountains and the sea.

contextUnits.zh: 不圖此心不遂，沒有餘恨，命也奈何！」

translations.literal: Did not expect this heart not to succeed; dying there is surplus regret—fate it—what to do!”
translations.idiomatic: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”
